prerequisites: Circuit theory with its main laws and theorems, both in direct and alternating current and in steady and transient regimes.
Basic electronics, both analog and digital and A/D conversion.
Basic instrumental concepts (noise, error, common mode, etc.)

learning_outcomes.text: Know the standards that electronic equipment must comply with to guarantee the safety of its users.
learning_outcomes.code: CG1, CG2, CG5, CG7, CG12 y CG13

learning_outcomes.text: Know the electromagnetic compatibility standards that equipment connected to the electrical network must comply with in relation to the injection of low-frequency harmonics into said network. Be able to measure said harmonics and propose solutions to ensure compliance with the standards.
learning_outcomes.code: CG1, CG2, CG5, CG7, CG12 y CG13

learning_outcomes.text: Know the standards that electronic equipment must comply with to guarantee its resistance against external physical actions, such as impacts, humidity, salinity, thermal cycles, etc.
learning_outcomes.code: CG1, CG2, CG5, CG7 y CG13

learning_outcomes.text: Plan the complete assembly of a simple electronic equipment.
Design a ventilation system (natural and forced) in simple electronic equipment.
Design printed circuit boards and plan their assembly.
Define a test process for a simple electronic equipment.
Document the circuitry used in electronic equipment.

syllabus_topics: Basic implementation of electronic systems on printed circuit boards (PCB)
Types of PCB, characteristics and applicable regulations
Gerber, BOM and Pick & Place files
Verification and testing of printed circuit boards
Thermal considerations in the design of electronic systems
Ventilation and cooling of electronic systems
Electromagnetic interference (EMI) and electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) in LF
Reduction of emitted interference and immunity to interference
Testing of electronic systems. EMI/EMC regulations
Advanced PCB design and wiring of electronic systems
PCB design for hostile EMI environments
Basic concepts: enclosures, damage and protections
Safety of people in handling electronic systems

Practical project to be carried out during the semester consisting of the development of an electronic system on which theoretical contents are developed: design and assembly of printed circuits, operational integration with the rest of the subsystems and verification of its operation. This work will be carried out in small groups.

assessment_methods.method: Laboratory practice monitoring (Planning, task assignment, milestone evaluation, partial reports)
Final project evaluation (Requirement fulfillment, additional functionalities, final report, oral presentation)

assessment_rules: For ordinary calls, the final grade is calculated as 25% for lab practice monitoring, 45% for the final project, and 30% for a written theoretical exam. For extraordinary calls, the theoretical part is 30% via written exam and the practical part is 70%. If the project was done, the same method as ordinary call is used for the practical part; otherwise, the practical grade is split equally between a practical exam and a design report. For differentiated evaluation, the theoretical part is 50% via written exam and the practical part is 50% via a comprehensive design report. To pass under differentiated evaluation, the average of both parts must be 5 points or higher, and the minimum score for each part must be 4 points. If the average is above 5 but either block is below 4 points, the final grade will be 4 points.
